candidate_relations.reason: Irritant contact dermatitis is a common peristomal differential without acantholysis or desmoglein antibodies.
Ileostomy complication is a parent surgical-site label missing pemphigus vulgaris.
Bullous pemphigoid is a subepidermal immunobullous disease, incompatible with suprabasal acantholysis and desmoglein antibodies.
Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita is a different subepidermal autoimmune blistering disease.
Paraneoplastic pemphigus is a different severe multi-mucosal pemphigus variant not required by this isolated peristomal lesion.
IgA pemphigus conflicts with intercellular IgG/C3 and IgG desmoglein ELISA.
Crohn disease complication is the underlying bowel context, not the immunobullous diagnosis.
Peristomal skin complication is a parent local label missing pemphigus vulgaris.
Autoimmune skin disorder is a parent category missing PV and peristomal localization.
Autoimmune bullous disease is the correct family missing PV and peristomal localization.
Pyoderma gangrenosum is a major peristomal ulcerative differential with incompatible immunofluorescence.
Peristomal pyoderma gangrenosum is the leading peristomal ulcer mimic, not pemphigus vulgaris.
Pemphigus vulgaris is the correct immunobullous disease but omits the required peristomal localized scope.
Pemphigus foliaceus is a superficial Dsg1-dominant pemphigus; suprabasal splitting and high Dsg3 indicate PV.
IgG autoantibody-mediated disease is a mechanism parent missing PV.
Linear IgA bullous dermatosis is a different immunobullous disease.
Skin infection is unlikely with repeatedly negative cultures.
Pemphigus is the parent immunobullous group missing vulgaris subtype and peristomal localization.
Crohn disease-related skin manifestation is a competing peristomal process, not PV.
Epidermal erosion is a histologic finding, not the diagnosis.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate; peristomal localized pemphigus vulgaris is more specific than any listed label
